evidence.observation: Barrel entry surface of MemoryCore's core. Line 25 re-exports `TdaiCore` (the host-neutral facade) together with its `TdaiCoreOptions`; every recall/capture/commit path in the fake-client contract is reached through this public facade, so the ordering rule the demo proves must hold here.

The core barrel also re-exports the client surface the task names as 'fake': `MockCredentialProvider` (line 56), `StaticCredentialProvider` (57) and `CachedCredentialProvider` (58). `MockCredentialProvider` is the deterministic fake client for local dev / unit tests, and `CachedCredentialProvider` is the real commit-after-effect client whose behavior the demo models.

Doc comment plus declaration (line 178) of the promise gate for the one-shot scheduler-start sequence. It explicitly rejects a plain boolean because it can be flipped to `true` before the awaited start completes, and states the in-flight promise is kept as the success sentinel only once it resolves — i.e. no success state is committed before the effect completes.

The concrete gate. Concurrent callers coalesce on `this.schedulerStartPromise` (1192); the async body awaits the checkpoint read and `scheduler.start(...)` (1198-1205) before the promise settles; the `.catch` at 1213-1215 clears the gate on rejection so the failure stays observable and a retry can run, while success keeps the resolved sentinel.

Turn commitment awaits `this.storeReady` and then `await this.ensureSchedulerStarted()` (413-414) before `performAutoCapture(...)` runs, so no capture/success is committed while the store/start effect is still pending.

The fake client itself: returns fixed placeholder credentials from `getCosCredential()` (44-46) and has a no-op `invalidate()`. No async effect and no hidden state, which makes it a safe deterministic stand-in for the 'fake client operation' in the test.

Cached client read path: a cached success short-circuits only when `!isExpired()` (106); otherwise it creates one shared in-flight `this.fetchPromise = this.refresh()` (112) that concurrent callers await and that is cleared in `finally` (118). Success is never returned from a still-pending effect.

The commit point: `this.cached = credential` is assigned only after `await this.fetcher()` resolves (154-155). On failure the client warns and serves the prior committed value if one exists (161-163), otherwise it re-throws the original error (165) so failure remains observable rather than being converted into a success.

Executable model of the `ensureSchedulerStarted` gate: `run()` returns one shared in-flight promise, increments `committed`/writes state only inside the `.then` after `await this._effect()` resolves, and the `.catch` records the failure and clears the gate so a retry is possible.

Executable model of `CachedCredentialProvider`: `get()` coalesces concurrent callers onto one `_refresh()`, `cached` is assigned only after the awaited fetcher resolves, and a failed fetch is re-thrown when there is no stale value — mirroring the commit-after-effect and observable-failure contract.

claims.claim: The public core surface that this contract is exercised through is the `MemoryCore/src/core/index.ts` barrel, which re-exports the `TdaiCore` facade and the storage/credential clients (`MockCredentialProvider`, `CachedCredentialProvider`) used as the deterministic fake and the real commit-after-effect client.

TdaiCore commits a success sentinel for the scheduler-start operation only after the awaited effect (checkpoint read + `scheduler.start`) completes: `ensureSchedulerStarted` stores the in-flight promise and `handleTurnCommitted` awaits it before any capture runs, so no success state is visible while the operation is pending.

Failure of the core gate stays observable: `ensureSchedulerStarted` clears `schedulerStartPromise` on rejection (retryable) and `initialize()`/the start path surface store-init failure via `logger.error` instead of silently succeeding.

The cached client commits its success state (`this.cached = credential`) only after `await this.fetcher()` resolves, and a failed fetch is re-thrown when there is no prior committed value, so failure cannot be mistaken for success.

`MockCredentialProvider` is the deterministic fake client for local development and unit tests; it performs no async effect and returns fixed credentials, which is what makes it suitable as the fake stand-in for the operation under test.

The executable demo `.prale-eval/contract/fake-client-operation.test.mjs` proves both halves of the contract against those semantics: success is committed strictly after the fake effect completes (no commit while pending), concurrent callers coalesce onto a single effect and a single commit, and failure is propagated/observed with zero commits on the failure path and retry possible afterward.

conclusion: MemoryCore's core exposes the exact contract the task asks to demonstrate. `TdaiCore.ensureSchedulerStarted` (core/tdai-core.ts) stores the in-flight scheduler-start promise as the success gate so concurrent callers await the same effect and no success is committed before it resolves; `handleTurnCommitted` awaits that gate plus `storeReady` before capturing; and failure clears the gate and is surfaced. The storage credential client encodes the same rule: `CachedCredentialProvider.refresh` commits `this.cached` only after `await this.fetcher()` resolves and re-throws when there is no stale fallback, while `MockCredentialProvider` is the deterministic fake client. The dependency-free executable demo models these two shapes (OperationGate, CoalescingFakeClient) and passes 7/7 cases: no success state is committed while the fake effect is pending, commit ordering is effect-then-success, concurrent callers share one effect and one commit, and failure is observable with zero commits and a working retry. This is a contract claim about the demonstrated operation semantics, not a full runtime import of the TypeScript sources (see validation notes).
